correctness.rationale: For every a>=2 and b>=c>=1 the fixed priority policy has a transient three-state matrix. Cramer determinants give a nonnegative b-c factor for H_C-H_B and an explicitly positive four-polynomial expression for H_A-H_C. Each claimed polynomial identity is checked by 343 exact evaluations and a proven degree bound <=6 per variable, yielding an all-parameter identity; 45 distinct finite full-vertex chains give independent exact-rational checks. The verified ordering satisfies the Bellman minimum conditions and implies optimality against all adaptive policies.

value.rationale: Complete tripartite graphs are the first complete multipartite family with genuine competition between two distinct non-target neighbor classes. The theorem resolves their graph-distance tie uniformly by part sizes and replaces parameter-by-parameter optimal-control computation with one fixed optimal priority and an exact three-state rational system. It proves strictness and the equal-size boundary throughout an infinite natural family; the result is not merely finite enumeration or a restatement of Bellman optimality.
